<!-- Generated by esquadro docs from the blueprint's manifest: do not edit. -->

A limit of requests a minute per client, answered with rate_limited (429) and Retry-After past it. It counts in memory: it holds for one instance of the service. An entity may also limit how many records each person creates (@rate_limit(create "10/h")), counted in the database.

```esquadro
blueprint rate_limit
```

## Works with

- **Requires** [http](../http/): the app must use them too.
- **Works with** [i18n](../i18n/) when the app uses them.

## Options

| Option | Type | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `per_minute` | int | `120` | Requests a minute each client may make; 0 turns the limit off. &lt;APP>_RATE_LIMIT overrides it. |

```esquadro
blueprint rate_limit {
  per_minute 120
}
```

## Environment variables

Read when the app starts; see [Environment variables](/esquadro/language/environment/).

| Variable | Type | Value | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<APP>_RATE_LIMIT` | int | the per_minute option | Requests a minute each client may make; 0 is no limit. |

## Annotations

| Where | Key | Type | |
|---|---|---|---|
| entity | `create` | string | How many records each person may create, as N/min, N/h or N/d: @rate_limit(create "10/h"). A person is a principal of the realm that owns the records (the owner rule of security), and what they created is what they own, created in the period, counted in the database: it holds for every instance of the service. Past it, rate_limited (429) with Retry-After; an import counts each record it creates. |

An annotation is written `@rate_limit(key value)` on the element.
